turns.response: You accrue **2.5 calendar days per month** (30 days/year) on active duty. Max carry-over is 60 days at the end of each fiscal year — any excess is lost unless protected by Special Leave Accrual (SLA). — AR 600-8-10, para 2-3a

turns.message: Who can approve emergency leave for one of my soldiers, and for how many days?
turns.response:
**Your unit commander (or approved designee) is the approval authority for emergency leave**, up to the following limits:

- **Up to 30 days** of emergency leave — approved by the unit commander or designated representative.
- **Up to an additional 30 days** of advance/excess leave may be combined, for a **total absence of up to 60 days**.
- **Beyond 60 days** — must be forwarded through next higher HQ to Commander, HRC (AHRC–PDP–P) for approval.

Accrued leave is charged first; if exhausted, it can be combined with advance leave, then excess leave. Red Cross verification is helpful but **cannot be the sole reason for disapproval**.

— AR 600-8-10, para 4-5

turns.message: I'm in the Navy. Is the day I depart on leave charged as a day of leave?
turns.response:
It depends on what time you depart. Per Navy policy:

- **Before end of normal working hours** → departure day **is charged** as a day of leave.
- **After end of normal working hours** → departure day is **not charged**; it counts as a duty day.
- **On a regular day off (weekend/holiday)** → leave may commence anytime, and **one of those non-duty days will be charged** as leave.

— MILPERSMAN 1050-090, para 3

turns.message: What's the maximum number of leave days I can sell back over my whole career?
turns.response:
**60 days** is the maximum leave you can sell back over your entire military career (per 37 USC § 501, effective 10 Feb 1976).

As an enlisted Soldier, you may also exercise a **one-time sell back** of up to 30 days if you'd otherwise lose leave accumulated beyond 120 days — but that counts toward your 60-day career cap. Officers and warrant officers are not eligible for the one-time sell back.

— AR 600-8-10, para 3-5; 37 USC § 501
